subject: US-WEST Reserved Pool Service Degradation — remediation & closure
participants_external: sarah.lee@novacart.ai (Sarah Lee, Novacart Head of Platform)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: ops@novacart.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, camila.reyes@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate notification: us-west reserved pool service degradation

Hi Sarah / Novacart team,

Short update and immediate context — we want to be transparent and give next steps.

What happened (brief): Between 2028-03-04 23:05 UTC and 2028-03-05 00:40 UTC your reserved GPU pool in us-west experienced sustained saturation that led to elevated latency and intermittent 502s for a subset of requests routed to that pool.

Customer impact we observed: ~6% error rate on generation endpoints for your production cluster, average tail P99 latency increased from 140ms to 1.2s, and a small number of long-running requests were retried by our edge leading to duplicate tokens in logs.

Immediate mitigation we applied: at 23:12 UTC we enabled burst routing to shared capacity, temporarily increased headroom for your reserved pool, and adjusted autoscaler warmup thresholds to avoid under-provisioning while the post-incident analysis runs.

Next steps we are committing to now:
- Deliver an evidence package (logs, autoscaler traces, and allocator snapshots) by EOD Pacific today. (attached)
- Provide a short postmortem with RCA and corrective actions within 48 hours.
- Offer a one-time service credit to account for the impact window; we will propose numbers after internal review.

Why this is happening (short hint): Our preliminary analysis points to a warmup mis-evaluation during a coordinated burst from two heavy workloads which reduced effective headroom in the reserved allocator. We are still collecting traces and will confirm root cause.

I'm cc'ing Ben and Camila from Customer Ops and Aditya from Platform so we can coordinate credits and the remediation timeline. I'll follow up with the evidence bundle and a draft RCA.

Apologies for the disruption — we recognize the impact and are prioritizing this.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: service-attach-logs.txt (log excerpts), novacart_session_sample.json (session snippet)

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@novacart.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 10:03:41 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate notification: us-west reserved pool service degradation

Thanks for the quick update, Marissa.

We saw the same errors on our end and had a handful of requests timeout. Two quick asks while you investigate:

1) We need an ETA on the full RCA and the list of mitigations you will put in place to prevent recurrence — our engineering leadership will want to review before our weekly ops sync.
2) What is Redwood's initial position on credits for production-impact incidents? We need a formal number and a timeline for application toward our next invoice.

Also can you confirm whether any customer data was exposed or routed outside our reserved pool during the burst? Data separation is a hard requirement for our compliance team.

Appreciate the transparency — please loop in any additional folks if helpful.

— Sarah
Sarah Lee
Head of Platform, Novacart

- Priority: finalize evidence bundle and confirm/no data egress.
- Aditya: can your team confirm whether allocator rebalancing code pushed last week affected warmup logic? If so we need a rollback candidate and a timeline for fix. Please include a short diff and the autoscaler trace windows (23:00-00:45 UTC).

I'll take point on the internal postmortem doc and prepare the remediation backlog for engineering.

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@novacart.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, camila.reyes@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: US-WEST reserved pool: post-incident update, evidence and credits

Hi Sarah,

Thank you again for your patience. Per our commitments, please find our post-incident delivery and next steps below.

What we are delivering now (attached and linked):
- Evidence package: novacart_evidence_package_20280305.zip (allocator snapshots, autoscaler traces, request traces, and curated log excerpts).
- Postmortem (draft): postmortem-dedicated-pool-20280305.pdf — includes timeline, RCA, and planned remediation work.
- Short video walkthrough (internal link): https://drive.google.com/fake/postmortem-novacart-20280305

Confirmed findings (summary):
- Root cause: an interaction between a recent autoscaler warmup heuristic change (rolled on 2028-03-02) and concurrent burst traffic from two internal workloads. The heuristic under-estimated warmup time for our reserved allocator which allowed the pool to appear 'ready' before actual GPU readiness metrics stabilized.
- Impact: brief under-provisioning that lasted ~95 minutes and elevated error/latency for a small fraction of traffic.
- Data separation: we confirm no customer data left the reserved pool nor were customer requests routed to other customers' reserved pools. During mitigation we routed to shared burst capacity but only to Kubernetes nodes hardened for routing without data egress; all request logs are included in the evidence package.

Immediate corrective actions already implemented:
- Rolled back the warmup heuristic change at 00:50 UTC.
- Temporarily increased reserved pool minimum headroom for burst windows while we validate the fix.
- Added additional autoscaler telemetry to capture readiness windows and failure modes.

Planned engineering work (next 30 days):
- Automated warmup tests in canary with synthetic warm-up traffic.
- Improved allocator invariants to prevent 'ready' state until GPU readiness is within safe thresholds.
- Additional alerting on rapid headroom consumption and coordinated-burst detection.

Credits and next steps:
- We propose a one-time billing credit equal to 20% of your reserved-capacity charge for the impacted hours (approx. X USD). If that is acceptable we'll apply the credit to your next invoice; Ben will confirm the exact amount and ledger entry by close of business tomorrow.
- We'll follow up with a 30-day remediation status and close the incident once fixes are merged and validated.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute call with Aditya and Ben to walk through any technical details with your platform team — propose Wed 03/07 10:00 PT or Thu 03/08 08:00 PT.

Apologies again for the disruption — we take this seriously and will share final postmortem updates as we close remediation tasks.

Best regards,

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: novacart_evidence_package_20280305.zip (zip, 18 MB), postmortem-dedicated-pool-20280305.pdf (6 pages), service-attach-logs.txt (excerpt)
